metadata.title: Signal Representations on Graphs: Tools and Applications

extraction_notes.note: Duplicate \label keys: thm:BLvsGS (Theorems 1 and 2), thm:GNNS (Theorems 4 and 5), thm:sparse (Theorem 9 and Corollary 1), eq:nonlinear_approx ((4) and (8)); refs resolve to the first. The proof of Theorem 11 cites thm:sparse but uses Corollary 1's 2T bound, so a CP1->PP12 edge was added by hand.
Section 5.3.1 repeats the nonlinear-approximation paragraph and equation (8) verbatim from (4), and repeats the NMSE formula unnumbered; only the first copies are nodes.

Labelled but unnumbered displays (eq:PLS, eq:C, eq:Delta, eq:trend_filtering) appear as equation facts; following the rule that unnumbered displays are not nodes, they stay inside their containing nodes. The two \eqref{eq:PLS} occur in experiment prose that is not a node.
One sentence (joined by semicolons) introduces V_L, V_P and V_W; kept as one definition because splitting would break the whole-sentence rule.
These prose nodes start right after a \mypar{...} paragraph heading macro, which the boundary check reports as mid-sentence; the statements start at the first word of the paragraph text.
Theorem 12 concludes P(Reject) <= delta under H_1 (presumably meant >= 1-delta), and Theorem 2's condition uses lambda_k with lowercase k; copied verbatim.
The classical time-frequency uncertainty principle is stated only in words with citations; kept as an external theorem (generalized by Theorem 5) rather than as an applied citation.
The three relaxed partition methods adapt cited techniques (spectral clustering, balance cut of a spanning tree, k-means); given origin paper as the paper's own relaxations of problem (7).

The case studies (coauthor network, SIS epidemics, SO2 change detection), dataset descriptions, figures and the author table are not extracted; only headline experimental findings are numerical claims.
Theorem 6 says it was 'shown in the previous section'; the prose paragraph checking the MRA requirements, which comes before the theorem, is taken as its proof.

\end{eqnarray}

The balance node partition the spanning tree into two subtrees with the closet number of nodes. We remove the balance node from the spanning tree, the resulting largest connected component form a children local set and the other nodes including the balance node forms the other children local set. nodes.statement: The third one is based on the 2-means clustering. We first randomly select 2 nodes as the community center and assign every other node to its nearest community center based on the geodesic distance. We then recompute the community center for each community by minimizing the summation of the geodesic distances to all the other nodes in the community and assign node to its nearest community center again. We keep doing this until the community centres converge after a few iterations. This method is inspired from the classical k-means clustering; it also guarantees that two children local sets are connected, but does not guarantees that they have the same number of nodes. In general, the proposed construction of local sets does not restrict to any particular graph partition algorithm; depending on the applications, the partition step can also be implemented by many other existing graph partition algorithms.

We use the multiresolution decomposition of the local sets as shown in Section~. Instead of obtaining a full decomposition tree, we partition the local sets until we obtain m leaf local sets. Those local sets may not be in the same decomposition level , but the union of them still cover the entire space. For the local sets in the same level of the decomposition tree, we first partition the one that has the largest number of nodes. For each leaf local set, we choose a center that has the minimum summation of the geodesic distances to all the other nodes in the leaf local set. The main idea is that we approximate a bandlimited signal in the original graph by using bandlimited signals in subgraphs. Based on the eigenvectors of graph Laplacian matrix, we define the bandlimited space, where each signal can be represented as $\mathbf{x} = \mathrm{V}_{(K)} \mathbf{a},$ where $\mathrm{V}_{(K)}$ is the submatrix of $\mathrm{V}$ containing the first $K$ columns in $\mathrm{V}$. We can show that this bandlimited space is a subspace of the total pairwise smooth space $\{\mathbf{x}: \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L} \mathbf{x} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} \}$. 

\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L} \mathbf{x} 
\  = \  \sum_{i,j \in \mathcal{E}} \mathrm{W}_{i,j} (x_i - x_j)^2
\\
& = & \sum_{S_c} \sum_{i,j \in \mathcal{E}_{S_c}} \mathrm{W}_{i,j} (x_i - x_j)^2  + \sum_{i,j \in (\mathcal{E} / \cup_{c} \mathcal{E}_{S_c}) } \mathrm{W}_{i,j} (x_i - x_j)^2
\\
& = &  \sum_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} + \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x} \ \leq \    \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x},
\end{eqnarray*}
where $\mathrm{L}_{S_c}$ is the graph Laplacian matrix of the subgraph $G_{S_c}$ and  $\mathrm{L}_{S_c}$ stores the residual edges, which are cut in the graph partition algorithm.


Thus, $\{\mathbf{x}: \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L} \mathbf{x} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} \}$ is a subset of $\bigcup_{S_c}  \{\mathbf{x}_{S_c}: \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x}  \}$; that is, any  total pairwise smooth graph signal in the whole graph can be precisely represented by total pairwise smooth graph signals in the subgraphs.

In each local set, when we use the bandlimited space 
$\{ \mathbf{x}: \mathbf{x} = {\mathrm{V}_{S_c}}_{(K)} \mathbf{a} \}$ to approximate the space $\{\mathbf{x}_{S_c}: \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \leq   c \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \}$, the maximum error we suffer from is $c \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathbf{x}_{S_c} / \lambda^{(S_c)}_{K+1}$, which is solved by the following optimization problem,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&	\max_{\mathbf{x}}  \left\|  \mathbf{x} - \mathrm{V}_{S_c} \mathrm{V}_{S_c}^T \mathbf{x} \right\|_2^2
	\\
&&	{\rm subject~to:}~   \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x} \leq   c  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x}.
\end{eqnarray*}
In other words, in each local set, the maximum error to represent $ \{\mathbf{x}_{S_c}: \mathbf{x}_{S_c}^T \mathrm{L}_{S_c} \mathbf{x}_{S_c} \leq  \lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x}   \}$ is 
$(\lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x})/\lambda^{(S_c)}_{K+1}$. Since all the local sets share the variation budget of $\lambda_K \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x}$ together, the maximum error we suffer from is $\epsilon_{\rm par} \left\| \mathbf{x} \right\|_2^2 = (\lambda_K  \mathbf{x}^T \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}^T \mathrm{L}_{\rm cut} \mathbf{x})/ \min_{S_c} \lambda^{(S_c)}_{K+1}$.



In Theorem~\ref{thm:sparse}, we have shown that we need at most $2 T \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{PC}} \right\|_0$ local sets to represent the piecewise-constant template of $\mathbf{x}$. Since we use at most $K$ eigenvectors in each local set, we obtain the results in Theorem~\ref{thm:PPL}.

\label{thm:PPL_Detect}
We consider statistically testing the null and alternative hypothesis,
\begin{eqnarray*}
H_0 &:& \mathbf{y} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 \mathrm{I}), 
\\
H_1 &:&  \mathbf{y} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x}, \sigma^2 \mathrm{I}),~\mathbf{x} \in \mathrm{PBL}_{\mathrm{V}_L}(C,K).
\end{eqnarray*}
We solve the following optimization problem
\begin{eqnarray*}
   \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* &  = &   \arg \min_{\mathbf{a}}  \left\| \mathbf{y} - \mathrm{D}_{\rm LSPS} \mathbf{a} \right\|_2^2   
   \\
   && {\rm subject~to~}  \left\| \mathbf{a} \right\|_0 \leq 2KT  \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0,
\end{eqnarray*}
by using the matching pursuit algorithm. We reject the null if $\left\| \mathbf{a}_{\mathbf{y}}^* \right\|_{\infty} > \tau$. Set $\tau = \sigma \sqrt{2 \log(KNT/\delta)}$. If
$$
\frac{\left\| \mathbf{x} \right\|_2}{\sigma} \geq C \sqrt{2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0 }  \sqrt{8 \log(\frac{KNT}{\delta})},
$$
where $C = \max_{ |\Omega| \leq 2KT \left\| \Delta \mathbf{x}_{\rm PC} \right\|_0  } \left\| (\mathrm{D}_{\rm LSPS})_{\Omega} \right\|_2 /(1- \sqrt{\epsilon_{\rm par}}) $. Then under $H_0$, $\mathbb{P}({\rm Reject}) \leq \delta$, and under $H_1$, $\mathbb{P} ({\rm Reject}) \leq \delta$.
